column1: # sync-lanes.tsv — template for <data-dir>/connectors/sync-scheduler/lanes.tsv
# Contract: packages/core/contracts/sync-lanes.md (schema_version 1.1.0).
# No path editing needed: `bash packages/connectors/scripts/sync-scheduler.sh
# init` copies this file into your private data dir at
# connectors/sync-scheduler/lanes.tsv as-is — the {{...}} placeholders below
# resolve per tick, from the checkout whose scheduler is executing, per the
# contract's "## Placeholders" section. This template is not read directly
# by the scheduler.
# Columns (tab-separated; command is the remainder of the line, spaces ok,
# tabs forbidden):
#   lane               [a-z0-9-]+, unique within the file
#   interval_seconds   integer >= 60
#   enabled             true | false
#   command             invocation, run via /bin/bash -c under launchd's
#                       minimal environment (PATH is just
#                       /usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin — no shell profile).
#                       May contain {{REPO_ROOT}}, {{DATA_DIR}},
#                       {{PRIVATE_DATA_ROOT}}, {{STORE_DIR}}, {{CLAUDE_BIN}}.
# Blank lines and lines starting with # are ignored. A malformed row fails
# the whole file (fail-closed parsing) — see the contract for details.
# Active example — {{REPO_ROOT}} resolves at each tick to the checkout that
# owns this lane's data dir (the repo whose beeper-in package writes into
# this data dir's inbox/).
beeper
# Delivery lane (plan 33) — renders and sends fired wake-up batches via
# packages/connectors/scripts/deliver-tick.sh, the channel configured in
# <store>/profile.md ## Notify (beeper-self, gmail-self, or outbox-only).
notify
# Feedback lane (plan 34) — parses numbered replies to delivered cards out of
# the note-to-self chat. Deterministic shell, no model session, so it's
# cheap to run every tick; must run after the beeper lane above so a reply
# captured this tick is already on disk for it to parse. Ships enabled.
feedback
# Learn lane (plan 36 D) — walks a cursor over signals/feedback.jsonl,
# regenerates the learned regression evals via ingestion's
# feedback-to-evals.sh, and holds conflicting corrections for the user in
# <data-dir>/attention/learn-conflicts.tsv (never auto-resolved, never
# writes user-model.md). Deterministic shell, no model session; must run
# after the feedback lane so this tick's parsed replies are already in the
# ledger. Ships enabled; a 3-line digest lands in logs/learn.log.
learn
# Staleness lane (plan 41) — hourly deterministic check: a lane silent past
# 2x its interval, or a capture lane green-but-empty for 24h, gets one self
# wake-up (packages/attention/scripts/staleness.sh); delivered by the
# sweep's fire step + notify lane.
staleness
# Store commit lane (plan 41) — commits and pushes the private data repo
# every tick via store-sync.sh tick; quiet when clean; a non-git store is a
# no-op.
store-commit
# Attention-fire lane (plan 44) — hourly deterministic run of
# wakeup-queue.sh fire (defaults --today to the current UTC date) followed by
# acted-on; writes wakeups/fired/<ts>-batch.json, which the notify lane above
# delivers. No model session. user-ask entries are budget-exempt so ad-hoc
# reminders fire on their due date; signal/standing entries stay gated by
# signals/week-plan.json's budget. Conceptually this must run before notify,
# but each lane is an independent launchd job — the next notify tick
# (<=15 min) picks up whatever batch this tick produced.
attention-fire
# Attention-sweep lane (plan 44) — one headless model session per tick
# running the full daily-attention sweep skill
# (packages/attention/skills/sweep/SKILL.md): inbox filing -> signal-scan ->
# staleness -> fire -> acted-on -> calibrate -> deliver -> heartbeat. This is
# the lane that produces signal-derived suggestions (birthday, tier-drift,
# scheduling-intent...) rather than only user-asked reminders. Disabled by
# default because (a) it is a model session (cost), (b) before enabling,
# data/ingestion/debrief-filed.log must reflect what is already filed or step
# 1 re-files the whole inbox — run one /debrief batch in a live session
# first. Enable with the same three steps as the MCP lanes below (preflight,
# flip, re-install). The sweep skill is not exposed as a slash command, hence
# the prompt reads the SKILL file directly.
attention-sweep
column4: /bin/bash {{REPO_ROOT}}/packages/connectors/scripts/mcp-lane-tick.sh tick --claude-bin {{CLAUDE_BIN}} --prompt "Read {{REPO_ROOT}}/packages/attention/skills/sweep/SKILL.md and execute every step in order against store-dir {{STORE_DIR}} with today's date; print each step= log line" --allowed-tools "Bash,Read,Write,Edit,Skill,mcp__claude_ai_Google_Calendar__*,mcp__claude_ai_Gmail__*" --max-turns 120 --timeout-seconds 1800 --expect "step=heartbeat status=ok"

column1: # MCP lanes (plan 28) — gmail/calendar sync runs as a headless Claude
# session per tick, via packages/connectors/scripts/mcp-lane-tick.sh. These
# rows are disabled by default; before enabling:
#   1. Optional: export SPOMNI_CLAUDE_BIN=<path> to pin a specific claude
#      binary, or leave {{CLAUDE_BIN}} below to find `claude` on PATH.
#   2. Run: bash {{REPO_ROOT}}/packages/connectors/scripts/mcp-lane-tick.sh
#      preflight --claude-bin {{CLAUDE_BIN}} --lane gmail|calendar
#      and confirm it reports preflight-ok.
#   3. Flip enabled to true and re-run sync-scheduler.sh install.
# Interval rationale: each tick is a model session, not a free localhost
# call (unlike beeper's 900s), so intervals here are a cost decision —
# gmail hourly, calendar every 2 hours. Worst-case ceiling at these
# defaults: 24 + 12 = 36 model sessions/day.
gmail-in
calendar-in
